title: Why BI matters: deciding by data instead of by opinion

videos.script: In February, Helena Prado wants to enlarge the Contagem store. {{saturday}} She has seen it on Saturdays: the car park is full, the tills have queues, and it sells more than any other store. Everything she says is true. It still does not answer her question. {{question}} This lesson is about why experienced people still need numbers. Memory keeps what was vivid, not what was frequent, and the loudest voice in a meeting is not always the best informed. {{decision}} Then a test for when data is worth fetching at all. A decision has options, a deadline and a cost of being wrong, and an analysis is worth what it could change. {{sheet}} Then the sheet. You type nine stores, their sales and their floor area, and divide. Contagem drops from first to fourth. {{limits}} Last, what the table cannot settle: the next square metre, a store that closed, and the profit nobody measured. The data narrows the argument. Helena still decides.
